To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the size criterion is a good predictor of metastatic disease in patients with early stage OCC and that the size criterion can be refined.

the number of unnecessary follow-up aspirations can be reduced by more than 50% without increasing false negative rates if selection criteria for USgFNAC in the neck of patients with OCC are based on laterality, level, size and change of diameter.

the number of unnecessary USgFNAC aspirations can be reduced by half by using the selection criteria of ipsilateral neck, MAD of 5.0 mm in level II, 4.0 mm in other levels, and rapid change in diameter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the refinement of selection criteria of the lymph nodes that need to undergo USgFNAC during follow-up of early staged OCC.
the refinement of selection criteria for USgFNAC of the neck in patients with oral cavity cancer.
the refinement of selection criteria for follow-up aspirations in patients treated with transoral excision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

USgFNAC of the neck in patients with early-staged OCC can be performed on the side with the largest tumor, on lymph nodes with a minimum axial diameter of 5.0 mm at level II and 3.0 mm at other levels or larger, and on lymph nodes with rapid increase of diameter.

the selection of lymph nodes to be aspirated in patients with OCC during follow-up can be based on the following criteria: (i) ipsilateral side of the neck, (ii) MAD larger than 5mm in the level II and 3.5mm in other levels and (iii) rapid change of size.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the selection criteria of lymph nodes for aspiration cytology during the follow-up period of patients with OCC and initially clinically N0 necks can be reduced by using the following selection criteria: ipsilateral neck, MAD larger than 4mm, or rapid change of diameter in any neck level.
the selection criteria used in this study can be used in patients with early-staged OCC and initially cN 0 necks to perform follow-up aspirations by USgFNAc.

we can reduce the number of follow-up aspirations in patients who underwent transoral excision and observation policy of the neck without increasing false-negative results by using a more refined selection criteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of lymph nodes that need to aspirated during follow up in patients with early stage OCC and initially cN 0 necks can be refined.
selection of nodes for follow-up aspiration can be improved by taking into account the laterality and change of size of the nodes in the neck.

in patients with early stage oral cavity cancer and initially cN 0 necks, follow-up aspiration cytology can be restricted to the ipsilateral neck, and only in lymph nodes with minimal axial diameter of 5.0 mm in level II or larger than 4.0 mm in other levels or in lymph nodes with rapidly changing diameter.
